title: Same question, same rubric, scores written before anyone talks
takeaway: When every candidate answers the same question against the same anchors, the scores measure the candidates, not the conversations.
sources: When the questions differ, the scores measure the conversations.
Score each answer on a small scale, 1 to 4 works well because it removes the easy middle.
Collect every interviewer's scores before anyone speaks.
Structure constrains what you ask and how you judge, not how you behave.

data.heading: One past-behaviour question, scored
lines: Q: Tell me about a time you had to ship with a known bug.
What did you decide and why?
Fixed follow-up: What would you do differently?
Strong: names the trade-off, gives the reason, checked the outcome
Acceptable: a reasonable decision, but not the reasoning
Weak: no concrete example, or blames others
Score 1 to 4, recorded before the debrief

notes.note: The same question for every candidate for the role, in the same order
Follow-ups are allowed but fixed too
Anchors written before any interview, in observable terms
Independent scores; 1 to 4 removes the easy middle
